title: The minimum-degree conjecture for distance-preserving graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph, and let $\delta(G)$ denote its minimum degree. A graph is **distance preserving** if it has an isometric subgraph of every order from $1$ to $n$.

**Minimum-degree conjecture.** If

$$
\delta(G)>n/2,
$$

then $G$ is distance preserving.

Nussbaum and Esfahanian proved the stronger minimum-degree condition $\delta(G)\geq 2n/3-1$, so the conjecture remains open in the stated range.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.03615

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2015).
